claim_summary: Kyed reports, attributing it to multiple reports rather than his own sourcing, that A.J. Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain and will undergo an MRI on Thursday to determine how long he will be out.
notes: ORIGIN IS UNREGISTERED. The diagnosis traces to an NFL Network report by Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo sourced as 'sources told'; I could not retrieve their originating post, so origin_url points to the earliest published carrier I could identify and retrieve, ESPN's 'Sources:' story (Sep 10 2026 10:01 AM ET). THAT ESPN STORY IS ALSO A RELAY AND IS NOT ATTRIBUTABLE TO A REGISTERED SOURCE: its byline reads 'Multiple Authors', not Mike Reiss, and it credits NFL Network in its lede. NO ASSIGNED SOURCE INDEPENDENTLY SOURCED THIS DIAGNOSIS; Kyed says 'per multiple reports' and Perry says 'what's been reported as', both recirculation. Marked update rather than confirm because it adds reported severity on top of the official injury record in -009 while NOT corroborating it: per -010 Vrabel was asked directly and would not confirm a diagnosis, so this is not an official fact. Kyed's '3-to-6 weeks' is a general expectation for high ankle sprains, not a reported timeline for Brown; the ESPN relay cites 2-to-6. NO ASSIGNED SOURCE REPORTED AN EXPECTED ABSENCE SPECIFIC TO BROWN. The ESPN relay adds that X-rays showed no fracture. Perry's separate relay of the same origin is deliberately not rowed: one origin, one cluster. BROWN'S LINE: 3 receptions on 4 targets for 26 yards per official -006; the fourth target is the third-and-4 incompletion at 13:30 of the third quarter on which he was injured, per official -009, so it is not a drop or a coverage failure.

Brown's own reported availability status is in the -101 cluster, not here. BROWN'S LINE: his fourth and final target is the incompletion on which he was hurt at 13:30 of Q3 (official -006 and -009), not a target he failed to convert.

notes: Reported explanation of the target distribution measured in official -006; the distribution itself is not restated. Columnist interpretation filed as analysis; the individual play descriptions are firsthand. Callahan separately reports Doubs saw no target until the fourth quarter, and that multiple players told him postgame the final play was designed as a quick passing concept evidenced by Campbell and Moses cut-blocking at the snap; that sourced scheme claim is not rowed here. BROWN'S LINE: his fourth target is the injury play itself at 13:30 of Q3 (official -009), which is why Callahan's 'caught all three targets' phrasing and the official 3-of-4 are both accurate.

Take the 38.1 percent film figure. DO NOT CONFLATE THIS WITH LAZAR'S TWO STEVENSON SNAP FIGURES, which are not a revision at all: 57-of-67 is measured against statistical offensive plays and 60-of-71 against actual snaps, and both are correct on their own base (see -109 and official -013).
